title: Chapter 1 Quiz: Introduction to AI & Agents
description: Test your mastery of AI definitions, agent architectures, PEAS framework, search algorithms, and symbolic logic.

questions.question: What is the primary defining characteristic of an Artificial Intelligence system?
options: It can perceive, reason, learn, and act to achieve goals
It requires vacuum tubes to function
It operates strictly on static if-else trees
questions.explanation: AI encompasses systems capable of perception, reasoning, learning from data, and rational action.

questions.question: Narrow AI (ANI) systems can easily generalize their expertise to completely unrelated domains.
questions.explanation: False. Narrow AI is dedicated to a single specialized domain (e.g., chess or medical imaging) and cannot transfer to unrelated tasks.

questions.question: What was the core proposition of Alan Turing's 1950 'Imitation Game'?
options: A machine can be considered intelligent if a human interrogator cannot distinguish it from a human
questions.explanation: Turing proposed that conversational indistinguishability from a human is a practical criterion for machine intelligence.

questions.question: In the PEAS framework for designing an intelligent agent, what does the letter 'P' stand for?
questions.explanation: In PEAS, P stands for Performance Measure, which quantifies the agent's degree of success.

questions.question: Which component of an AI agent enables it to perceive its environment?
questions.explanation: Sensors receive signals and percepts from the external environment.

questions.question: For an autonomous delivery drone, which of the following is an Actuator?
questions.explanation: Propeller motors are actuators because they exert physical force to navigate the drone.

questions.question: A rational agent must possess complete omniscience and predict the future with 100% certainty.
questions.explanation: False. Rationality is about making the best expected decision given available percepts and objectives, not knowing the future.

questions.question: Which search algorithm always explores the shallowest unexpanded node first using a FIFO queue?
questions.explanation: Breadth-First Search (BFS) explores level-by-level using a FIFO queue, guaranteeing the shortest path on unweighted graphs.

questions.question: What is the evaluation function formula f(n) used in the A* search algorithm?
questions.explanation: A* calculates f(n) = g(n) + h(n), combining the exact path cost so far g(n) with the heuristic estimate to the goal h(n).

questions.question: A heuristic function h(n) is admissible if it never overestimates the true cost to reach the goal.
questions.explanation: True. Admissibility guarantees that A* tree search finds the optimal solution without overestimating cost.

questions.question: Which of the following environments is considered fully observable and deterministic?
questions.explanation: In Chess, the entire board state is completely visible at all times, and moves follow deterministic rules.

questions.question: In symbolic expert systems, what is the role of the Inference Engine?
options: Applying logical deduction rules to facts in the Knowledge Base
questions.explanation: The inference engine reasons over the knowledge base by applying logical rules to derive new facts or conclusions.

questions.question: Which inference strategy starts with observed data and continuously applies IF-THEN rules until a goal is derived?
questions.explanation: Forward chaining is data-driven, propagating forward from known premises to conclusions.

questions.question: Why did classical expert systems experience an 'AI Winter' and fail to solve complex real-world perception?
options: Because manually writing rules for millions of noisy edge cases was brittle and unscalable
Because internet bandwidth was too high
questions.explanation: Hand-crafted symbolic rules could not scale to the immense noise, uncertainty, and nuance of real-world sensory data.

questions.question: Artificial ______ Intelligence refers to a hypothetical AI capable of learning and solving any intellectual task a human can.
questions.explanation: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) denotes human-level flexibility across diverse cognitive domains.

questions.question: In Depth-First Search (DFS), the memory complexity is linear with respect to the maximum search depth.
questions.explanation: True. DFS only stores the current branch in memory, giving O(b*m) space complexity compared to BFS's exponential O(b^d).

questions.question: What is the key limitation of Breadth-First Search (BFS) on graphs with deep solutions?
options: It gets trapped in infinite cycles easily
Exponential memory consumption as depth increases
It cannot find the goal state
questions.explanation: BFS must hold all frontier nodes in memory, causing exponential RAM exhaustion on large state spaces.

questions.question: Which type of agent maintains an internal state to track aspects of the environment that cannot be viewed right now?
questions.explanation: Model-based reflex agents maintain internal models to handle partial observability.

questions.question: A vacuum cleaner that only looks at whether the current tile is dirty without checking past history is a Simple Reflex Agent.
questions.explanation: True. Simple reflex agents base decisions exclusively on the current percept, ignoring history.

questions.question: In heuristic search, what does Manhattan Distance measure between points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)?
questions.explanation: Manhattan Distance calculates grid-based distance along perpendicular axes: |x2 - x1| + |y2 - y1|.
